prerequisites: Knowledge provided in the basic courses of Electronic Measurements

learning_outcomes.text: Describe the architecture and operating principles of automatic measurement systems and data acquisition systems.
Understand the structure of a metrological chain and the role of the main components of a measurement system.
Understand the basic characteristics of the main communication interfaces for electronic instrumentation (IEEE 488, RS-232, RS-422, RS-449, RS-485, USB) and of VXI and PXI modular systems.
Understand the principles of virtual instrumentation and the LabVIEW development environment, with particular reference to the programming of instruments and data acquisition systems.
Design simple automated measurement systems based on application specifications.
Develop software applications in the LabVIEW environment for the acquisition, processing, and visualization of measurement data.
Program data acquisition devices and measurement instruments using the main communication interfaces.
Integrate hardware and software to create virtual instruments capable of automating experimental and measurement procedures.
Evaluate the most appropriate hardware and software solutions for implementing an automated measurement system.
Identify the main critical issues in communication between instruments, in device configuration, and in data acquisition.
Critically analyze the results obtained during experimental activities, identifying any anomalies and proposing corrective actions in simplified contexts.
Document design and experimental activities using appropriate technical language.
Present and discuss the design choices made and the solutions developed as part of the final project.
Collaborate effectively within a work group, contributing to the planning, development, and validation of the project.
Clearly communicate results, issues, and solutions related to the design of automatic measurement systems.
Independently acquire skills in using new software tools and data acquisition devices by consulting technical manuals and specialized documentation.
Stay up to date on developments in virtual instrumentation technologies and automated measurement systems.
Address simple design problems by integrating knowledge from the fields of electronic measurement, programming, and hardware-software interfacing.
Apply the methodologies learned to the development of similar applications in various contexts within information engineering.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of electronic measurement courses
Components of a measurement system and their functionality
Characteristics of automatic measurement systems and data acquisition systems
Definitions of automatic measurement system, data acquisition system, distributed measurement system
Elementary components of automatic and data acquisition systems: acquisition section, processing section, presentation section
Elementary concepts for the design of a data acquisition system
Electrical, mechanical and functional specifications of main interface systems
Fundamental characteristics of the LabVIEW development environment
Programming of IEEE 488 interface in LabVIEW
Programming of RS-232C interface in LabVIEW

assessment_methods.method: Completeness and accuracy of project solution
Clarity and completeness of presentation of theoretical concepts

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on an oral exam. Two-thirds of the grade will be based on the completeness and accuracy of the project solution, and one-third on the clarity and completeness of the presentation of theoretical concepts. The successful completion of the project work and the submission of the final technical report are required to take the exam.
bibliography: J.F. Coombs - Electronic Instrument Handbook - McGraw-Hill Pub. Co.
Lecture notes and lecture slides will be provided to the registered students via the learning management system Handy Unisannio
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Informatica (Computer Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
